niche.title: 8 Cranial Bones Mnemonic: Old People From Texas Eat Spiders | Skull Anatomy #shorts
niche.description:
Can you name all 8 cranial bones? One silly sentence does it: Old People From Texas Eat Spiders 🦴

O → Occipital: the back of your skull (the spinal cord exits through its foramen magnum)
P → Parietal: top and sides (a pair)
F → Frontal: your forehead
T → Temporal: right above your ears (a pair)
E → Ethmoid: tucked between your eye sockets
S → Sphenoid: the "keystone" that joins almost every other skull bone
6 names, but parietal and temporal come in pairs = 8 cranial bones.

Quick test: your spinal cord leaves the skull through which bone? Answer in the video.

niche.title: 6 Deep Hip Rotators Mnemonic: P-GO-GO-Q (Piriformis to Quadratus Femoris) #shorts
niche.description:
Can you name all 6 deep hip rotators? One word does it, top to bottom: P-GO-GO-Q 🍑

P → Piriformis (the top one, from the sacrum)
G → Gemellus superior
O → Obturator internus (its tendon runs between the two gemelli, "little twins")
G → Gemellus inferior
O → Obturator externus (hidden deep, behind quadratus femoris)
Q → Quadratus femoris (the bottom one)
All 6 run to the greater trochanter area of the femur and rotate the thigh outward (lateral rotation).

Quick test: which big nerve exits just below piriformis? Answer in the video.

The Only Bone That Touches No Other Bone: the Hyoid (Anatomy Fact) #shorts
niche.description:
This bone touches NO other bone 🤯 Meet the hyoid.

The hyoid bone is the only bone in your body that doesn't form a joint with another bone. It sits in the front of your neck at the level of C3, between your jaw (mandible) and your larynx, held up only by muscles and ligaments: suprahyoid muscles above, infrahyoid muscles below, and the stylohyoid ligaments.

Memory trick: "hyoid" means U-shaped, like the Greek letter upsilon.
Parts: 1 body + 2 greater horns + 2 lesser horns (old atlases say "cornu" = horn).

Quick test: what does the hyoid anchor? Answer in the video.

Stop accidentally stretching your sciatic nerve
niche.description:
Stop accidentally stretching your sciatic nerve ⬇️
.
When you have sciatica and feel tightness down the back of your leg, it's natural to want to stretch your hamstrings.
.
But your sciatic nerve is part of one long rope that runs from your brain, down your spinal cord, and into your foot and toes.
.
So when you move your head or your foot, you change how much stretch goes through the nerve.
.
If you tuck your chin and pull your toes toward you during a hamstring stretch, you're stretching the nerve more than the muscle. With sciatica, that can really aggravate your symptoms.
